findings.where: First screen (hero sheet), desktop and phone, and the whole page: the address strip at the foot of the sheet that the palette ('Pad yellow: the address strip') and texture notes describe, and the nav (Profile, Articles, Blog)
findings.fault: There is no way to reach Mark anywhere on the page. The first screen has no email address, no contact link and no yellow address strip, though the tile's own notes say one sits at the foot of the sheet. The nav has no Contact item. parts.txt lists no mailto link and no contact part. The page has no primary action, so after the portrait and the headline the visitor has nowhere to go.
findings.who_objects: The bank official who has decided they would like to talk to Mark finds no address and has to leave the site to look one up. The founder would object too: the brief's personal-advisor test requires 'one direct, personal way to reach him', with the address shown, and the brand sheet names getting in touch as the page's one action.

findings.where: Motion sketch section, the full-width lilac panel at the foot of the tile (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The motion sketch sits on a strong lilac fill. That hue is not in the palette, which is paper, grey, blue and pad yellow, and the palette says the ground is paper 'everywhere'. The panel is the loudest area on the whole page (in the overview it out-shouts the hero), and it makes the sober legal-paper direction look like a candy-coloured template.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges this tile against a brief of 'one soft ground, the house blue and grey as the only ink' and 'refined, never childish'. A senior official would read the pastel purple as off-brand and unserious next to a lawyer's paper.

findings.where: Article specimen: the subheads 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and 'Download'
findings.fault: The subheads are set in a heavy, wide grotesque. That is a third typeface the tile's own type pair does not name: it says Newsreader 500 for subheads and Public Sans for labels. The heavy wide sans breaks from the refined serif voice and reads as slick or techy, a jolt in the middle of Mark's essay.
findings.who_objects: The reader of Mark's article, for whom the subhead looks pasted in from another site. The founder too: the brief says nothing should read as 'in-your-face techy', and Angélique needs one stated subhead style she can repeat.

findings.where: Nav links Profile, Articles and Blog (parts p2–p4: #profile, #articles, #blog), and the Download link 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' (p5: #)
findings.fault: The nav items point to in-page anchors that do not exist on this page, and the one PDF download points to '#'. Each looks like a working link, but a click goes nowhere. The research names the PDF list as 'the product'.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to check Mark's publications before getting in touch clicks Articles or the lecture PDF and nothing happens. That reads as a broken site, which costs trust with a reader who is vetting an advisor.

findings.where: Palette row: the four swatches (outlined rectangle, rounded grey block, blue ellipse, yellow box with a blue edge)
findings.fault: Each swatch has a different shape: square, rounded, oval, and blue-outlined. None of the differences means anything. The oval looks playful, and the blue edge on the yellow swatch reads as a selected or focused state rather than a colour.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who reads the palette as the specification for the house look. Four arbitrary shapes suggest radius and outline rules the direction does not have, and the oval undercuts 'refined'.

findings.where: Article specimen title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'
findings.fault: The display title uses a straight typewriter apostrophe ('World's'), while the body and subhead use curly quotes. At this size the straight mark is very visible.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader of a lawyer's published writing, for whom a typewriter apostrophe in the largest line on the page looks unedited.

findings.where: Article specimen, Download row on desktop: link title on the left, 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' far right
findings.fault: The item's date and format sit a wide gap away from its title, level with the title's first line, so they read as a separate stray label rather than the facts of this download.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning a list of talks to find the newest one, who has to track across empty space to pair each date with its title.

findings.where: Motion sketch timing table at phone width
findings.fault: The four-column table is squeezed so the Element column wraps one or two words per line ('Mark's / line / settles: / opacity…'), turning a two-line description into a tall ragged column.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the tile on a phone, who has to piece the timing rows back together.
